general_background.title: Carboxylic-acid and carboxylate ligands
general_background.summary: Carboxylic acids and carboxylates can associate with metal-containing surfaces and solution species through their oxygen groups. The hydrocarbon part of a long-chain ligand can favour dispersion in a compatible solvent, while acid-base equilibria influence how its head group associates.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Solvent and transport
general_background.summary: A solvent carries dissolved species and transports heat through a reaction or dispersion. Solubility, viscosity and molecular interactions affect how precursors and ligand-coated particles move and mix.
